A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the G-proteins that mediate the regulation of Na+ channels in the apical plasma membrane of lung epithelial cells undergo changes during the perinatal period.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the G-proteins regulating 22Na+ channels in the neonatal lung apical membrane undergo a rapid change at birth.

the regulation of 22Na+ conductive uptake in AMV prepared from guinea pig lung undergoes significant changes following birth and by 5 days of age, the uptake of 22Na into these vesicles is predominantly regulated via PTX-sensitive Gialpha3.
Gialpha3 is likely to play an important role in regulation of conductance of 22Na+ in the apical plasma membrane of the lung.
